The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus and presents with severe metabolic acidosis, elevated β-hydroxybutyrate level, and trace ketones on urinalysis, which are characteristic findings of diabetic ketoacidosis.
The patient has a history of bilateral nonobstructive renal artery stenosis and presents with elevated creatinine levels, indicating chronic kidney disease.
The patient has a history of hypertension and presents with blood pressure readings, indicating hypertensive heart disease.

The patient presents with signs of infection, such as fever and metabolic acidosis, which could indicate sepsis, although the absence of hypoxia and other typical sepsis symptoms makes it less likely.
The combination of hyperglycemia, metabolic acidosis, and ketonuria can be explained by a state of diabetic ketoacidosis, which is a complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
The presence of bilateral nonobstructive renal artery stenosis and acute renal failure suggests a chronic kidney disease process that has been exacerbated by the current illness.
